dedupe_keys.name: solar power initiative using caltrans right of way final research report caltrans project p1253 2020

description: A December 2020 research report for the California Department of Transportation by Sarah Kurtz of UC Merced and a Texas A&M Transportation Institute team on developing solar power in Caltrans right-of-way (ROW). Contents: summaries of a literature review, interviews with other state DOTs, the rules and regulations that limit renewable energy facilities in the state ROW, a financial opportunities assessment of ownership and power purchase agreement options, best practices and a chapter on future solar technology; it cites a national estimate that ROW solar could produce up to 36 TWh a year, about 1,800 GWh a year for California, and works this into roughly 1 GW of systems. Coverage: California's state highway ROW, with lessons from other states. Format and access: a free 317-page PDF with appendices. Licence and cost: free; no licence was stated. Caveats: the potential figures are borrowed from an earlier study and not a site-by-site GIS inventory. Useful for capacity planning of roadside solar and grid connections and for adaptation planning where ROW generation supports highway loads. It relates to The Ray ROW solar mapping tool and the European roads and railways vertical solar case study in the catalogue.
